evidence.evidence_paraphrase: The nanoparticles are drop-cast onto silicon and dried before the analyte is subsequently drop-cast onto the nanoparticle film for Raman measurement.
Reproducibility is assessed from measurements at more than ten different sites on Ag@Au and Cu@Au nanoparticle films.
The paper reports concentration-dependent intensity changes without Raman-mode shifts, rather than a solution-to-dried paired spectral transformation.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper uses Ag-containing Au bimetallic nanoparticles and a dried SERS film, and it reports site-to-site intensity reproducibility, but its protocol does not compare the same analyte-mixed preparation in solution and after drying. It therefore does not establish the paired context-dependent change in normalized peak distribution or peak profile.

evidence.evidence_paraphrase: The introduction states that intensified local electromagnetic fields arise when nanoparticles are in close proximity, forming SERS hotspots.
The Ag@Au particles are described as Au-rich centers with Ag decorated on the surface, rather than polymer-separated Ag bridges with controlled gaps.
The paper attributes stronger Ag@Au SERS enhancement to silver plasmonic properties and sharp particle edges that accumulate free electrons and enhance the local field.
The observed SERS signals are attributed to hotspots from closely packed plasmonic metal nanoparticles.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper supports the general mechanistic relation that close proximity among plasmonic particles creates hotspots and that Ag-containing Au structures can produce stronger SERS responses. However, it does not study the polymer-separated Ag-bridge architecture or controlled variation of its inner/outer gap, and it does not establish a reproducible directional gap-size trend.
